flawed_step: Lines 0551-0559 (Section 4, final step of the proof of Theorem PreobZZ): the bound |M_chi(x,y_0)| << x*exp(-c(log x)^{3/5}(log_2 x)^{-1/5}) for X^c << x << X is asserted 'by an argument similar to that of Koukoulopoulos' with no proof. Every quantitative consequence of the section depends on it, and by the paper's own Section 1 the analogous unramified bound (line 0266, eq. PreobMxyassert) holds only *if* l_0 is 'the level' -- a hypothesis the paper explicitly declines to verify (lines 0268-0270). A secondary, concretely refutable defect is the stated formula for beta(n,y) at lines 0216-0219, which makes the basic identity (5) false.
counterexample: Concrete counterexample to the basic arithmetic identity (5) as literally stated (lines 0213-0219). Take y = 3 and X = 1 (any 1 <= X < 2 works). LHS: M(X,y) = sum over n <= X with P^-(n) > y or P^-(n/2) > y of mu(n). Only n = 1 qualifies (P^-(1) = infinity > 3), so M(1,3) = mu(1) = 1. RHS: floor(X/2)+1 = 1 and floor(X) = 1, so the right-hand side is the single term beta(1,3). The paper defines beta(n,y) = sum_{k=1}^{Omega(n)} (-1)^k d_k^*(n,y); since Omega(1) = 0 this is an empty sum, i.e. beta(1,3) = 0. Hence (5) asserts 1 = 0. The inversion theorem itself (line 0176) requires beta(1) = 1/alpha(1) = 1/alpha(1,y) = 1, so the displayed formula for beta(n,y) is simply wrong at n = 1. The same mismatch propagates to line 0227: for n = 1 and k = 2 the stated recursion reads d_2^*(1,y) = d_2'(1,y) - 2 d_1^*(1,y), i.e. 0 = 1 - 2*1 = -1, false; consequently F_{l,y}(s) is a combination of zeta^k(s)prod_{p<=y}(1-p^{-s})^k for 1 <= k <= l plus an omitted constant (k = 0) term, contrary to the claim on lines 0229-0230.
reasoning_summary: I checked the paper's verifiable machinery first and it is sound: (a) Theorem 1's beta is exactly the Dirichlet inverse of alpha -- I confirmed the closed form against the recursive inverse for n = p, p^2, p^3 with general alpha(1) = a, and the k >= 2 constraint 'n_i not in {1,n}' is equivalent to 'n_i > 1' since the factors multiply to n; (b) the X = 6 numerical example in Section 2 is correct -- the matrix entries a(n) = log n - d(n), the b_n (in particular b_4 = -(log2)^2+2log2-1 and b_6 = -2log2log3+3log2+3log3-4), and the numerical identity sum b_n Delta_(n) = -1.0001 = M(6); (c) the Euler-product identity on lines 0202-0205 does give U(X) = sum alpha(n,y) M(X/n,y), and beta(n,y) = sum_k (-1)^k d_k^*(n,y) for n > 1 -- I verified identity (5) numerically for y = 3 at X = 6, 10, 25, 35 (values -1, -1, -4, -3 on both sides); (d) the Section 4 contour manipulations (Mellin transform on line 0487, entirety of g_chi for even chi, the sigma = lambda bound giving e^{lambda+4}/(lambda-2) << X, the sigma = 0 shift giving |r_lambda(H)| << q^{3/2}, and the residue at s = 1+beta_0 giving U >> X^{1+beta_0}/log y_0) are all correct or harmlessly over-generous. So the refutation does not lie there. Where the argument breaks is that the concluding inequality beta_0 <= 1 - c/log q is derived entirely from an unproved black box (lines 0551-0559): granting that bound, the arithmetic does work out (one gets (1-beta_0)log X >> (log X)^{3/5}(log_2 X)^{-1/5} and, with log q asymptotic to (log X)^{2/5}(log_2 X)^{1/5}, exactly 1-beta_0 >> 1/log q), which shows how much weight the unjustified step carries -- it is of the same strength as the paper's own admittedly conditional (6). The independently checkable defect I can exhibit outright is the n = 1 failure of the stated beta(n,y) and of the recursion on line 0227, given above.
